rationale: Both responses pick the same top three (Zettelkasten, PARA/CODE and Evergreen Notes) and end with a sensible synthesis. A better meets the request for a comprehensive list of procedure-oriented frameworks. Its catalogue is broader and well categorized, covering classical reading and note methods, digital PKM, productivity-adjacent methods, taxonomic approaches and memory techniques. Its top-three summaries are written as explicit numbered procedures plus best practices, which matches the 'system of procedures' framing. B adds valuable Zettelkasten detail: Ahrens' popularization and the fleeting, literature and permanent note types. Its layered philosophy/method/organization/workflow diagram is a nice touch. However, B pads its list with tool conventions and restated principles rather than distinct frameworks. It also has factual slips, such as giving Luhmann's dates as 1960s-2012 while elsewhere saying he died in 1998, undercounting his books, and claiming Matuschak uses Obsidian. Neither credits Rheingold's original 'Tools for Thought'. A's minor attribution looseness is less damaging, so overall A is more comprehensive and more actionable.
